harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented port isolation between node2 and node3 on their shared L2 segment with node1 (192.168.50.0/24), verified the healthy baseline, restarted every node one at a time, and confirmed persistence and recovery of the isolation and connectivity afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected topology on all 3 nodes: node1 (SONiC) eth1, node2 enp8s0, node3 enp8s0 sit on one flat, unrouted L2/L3 segment (not switched through node1) provisioned with no IPs assigned.

Assigned static IPs on the shared segment: node1 eth1=192.168.50.1/24 (persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1, outside SONiC's managed INTERFACE table so interfaces-config.service does not clobber it), node2 enp8s0=192.168.50.11/24 and node3 enp8s0=192.168.50.12/24 (persisted via nmcli static profiles on 'Wired connection 2').
Captured a healthy baseline: full mesh reachability (node2<->node3, node2<->node1, node3<->node1) all working before any isolation rule was applied.

Since node2<->node3 traffic never transits node1 (confirmed empirically -- it's a flat shared segment, not a node1-mediated switch path), applied host-based isolation via firewalld persistent rich rules: node2 drops all traffic (any protocol) sourced from 192.168.50.12 (node3); node3 drops all traffic sourced from 192.168.50.11 (node2). Node1 is left unfiltered so both continue reaching it.
Verified isolation: node2<->node3 ICMP and TCP (SYN to port 22) both fail/time out in both directions; node1<->node2 and node1<->node3 ICMP succeed in both directions.

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id on all 3 nodes, restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (SONiC, one at a time, native `reboot`), polled each until exec access returned, confirmed each boot_id changed, and re-verified IP config, firewalld rich rule, SONiC docker container health, and the same isolation/reachability pattern held after each restart, finishing with a full three-node health and isolation re-check.

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy segment before isolation (node1<->node2<->node3 subnet reachability)
evidence.summary: Static IPs assigned on the shared 192.168.50.0/24 segment (node1 eth1 .1, node2 enp8s0 .11, node3 enp8s0 .12); full-mesh ping succeeded in all directions before any isolation rule existed.

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 cannot exchange traffic directly
evidence.summary: Persistent firewalld rich-rule drops added on node2 (source 192.168.50.12) and node3 (source 192.168.50.11); post-rule ICMP between node2 and node3 fails 100% both directions, and a raw TCP connect attempt from node2 to node3:22 times out (no RST), confirming protocol-agnostic drop.

evidence.requirement: Both node2 and node3 continue to reach node1 on the shared subnet
evidence.summary: node2->node1 and node3->node1 ICMP succeed with 0% loss after the isolation rules were applied; node1->node2 and node1->node3 also succeed.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7223d5b7...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-boot boot_id changed to 00c2c9bd...; recovered state shows enp8s0 IP retained, firewalld rich rule intact, node2->node1 reachable and node2->node3 still blocked.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e625b9a5...; reboot acknowledged; post-boot boot_id changed to b62a6aa5...; recovered state shows enp8s0 IP retained, firewalld rich rule intact, node3->node1 reachable and node3->node2 still blocked.

evidence.requirement: node1 (SONiC) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state including cluster membership/services
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4aba45d4...; reboot acknowledged; polled through downtime until boot_id changed to 688a02fd...; recovered state confirms eth1 static IP persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1, all SONiC docker containers (database, swss, bgp, syncd, teamd, sysmgr, eventd, radv, gbsyncd) back up healthy, and node1 reaches both node2 and node3.

evidence.requirement: Final cluster-wide state after all three restarts: isolation and reachability both still correct
evidence.summary: Post-restart full recheck: node1<->node2 and node1<->node3 both reachable; node2<->node3 still 100% blocked in both directions, confirming persistence of the port-isolation configuration across a full reboot cycle of all three nodes.

attempts.summary: Implemented port isolation between node2 and node3 on their shared L2 segment with node1 (192.168.50.0/24), verified the healthy baseline, restarted every node one at a time, and confirmed persistence and recovery of the isolation and connectivity afterward.
